prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a low-speed head-on collision in Katy, Texas, and has neck strain. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1135; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for agreeing to give this recorded statement. Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather just keep it to the accident, if that's alright.
Q: That's fine. We'll keep it brief. Can you tell me where the collision happened?
A: It was on a two-lane road in Katy, Texas, near a shopping center entrance.
Q: What time of day was it?
A: Late afternoon, maybe around four or five. It was still light out.
Q: Walk me through what happened.
A: I was heading east and slowing down for the turn lane. The other car came over the center line and hit me head-on. It wasn't going very fast, though. I'd guess maybe fifteen or twenty miles an hour.
Q: Did you apply your brakes before impact?
A: Yes, I braked hard, but there wasn't much room to stop.
Q: Were you wearing your seatbelt?
A: Yes, and the airbag didn't deploy, which I think is why I got the neck thing.
Q: Describe your injuries.
A: My neck is sore and stiff, mostly in the back and on the right side. I've got a headache some mornings too.
Q: Have you seen a doctor or other provider since the accident?
A: I went to urgent care the same evening, and I've been seeing a physical therapist twice a week since.
Q: Any prior neck or back problems you can recall?
A: Nothing serious. I had some stiffness a few years ago after lifting something, but it went away with stretching.
Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add?
A: Just that the other driver apologized at the scene. That's about it.
Q: Thank you. This concludes the statement.
